newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC quota compliance meeting gets underway.
newsitem.headline: OPEC quota compliance meeting gets underway.

text.p: OPEC's four-man quota compliance committee, briefed to examine recent OPEC member country crude output, started a scheduled meeting in Vienna on Wednesday morning, an OPEC official said.
The committee was chaired for the first time by Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh.
Libya's Abdalla al-Badri, Nigeria's Dan Etete and OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman also were in attendance.
The routine meeting was not expected to recommend any new methods for monitoring OPEC output, OPEC delegates said.

Several member countries are pumping over their allotted OPEC quotas but world demand has easily absorbed the excess in recent months, even at international market prices running around five-year highs.
In June OPEC raised its ceiling to 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) to allow for the eventual resumption of partial Iraqi exports under a U.N. oil-for-food exchange.
But secondary media sources monitored by OPEC put August production at 25.77 million bpd, despite the postponement of Iraqi sales, OPEC's Secretariat said last week.
